# Agent registry

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P2 · Proven identity](../README.md#phase-2--proven-identity) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:agent-registry` · **Epic:** [#70](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/70) · **Tickets:** 7 (4S 3M)

Adds a control-plane registry of agents so the token service knows which agents exist, which public keys authenticate them and which user groups may delegate to them. Workers receive each agent's status and key thumbprints on the existing /policy long-poll, can be pinned to a registered agent id, and deny all traffic for an agent an admin has disabled. The per-agent identity mode stays in the P1 settings field, so there is one source of truth for it.

## How we build it

- Data model: new package internal/agentreg on the W-P1-SSO-01 cpstate DB, migration `agents/0001`. Table `agents(id PK, display_name, owner_iss, owner_sub, owner_email, allowed_groups_json, allowed_scopes_json, status active|disabled, revision INTEGER, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by)` plus `agent_keys(jkt PK, agent_id, kid, alg, jwk_json)`, so a key thumbprint can belong to only one agent. There is no identity_mode column and no environments column. Rows are never deleted and ids are never reused, so audit rows and token references stay resolvable. The registry holds at most `config.MaxRegisteredAgents` (1000) agents.
- Agent ids: new `agentid.ValidID` with pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$`, compared case-sensitively and exactly. It accepts `agent:<port>` from agentid.PortBindingIdentifier and typical existing `agents[].id` values, and it rejects the P1 sentinel `!identity-scoped`. config.validateAgents keeps accepting any non-empty id; ids that fail ValidID only produce a warning there, so existing YAML still loads.
- Keys: public keys are accepted only as JWKs and parsed with the internal/keys JWK code and RFC 7638 thumbprint from W-P2-KEYS-01, so agentreg, the token service (W-P2-TOKX-01) and workers (W-P2-WBND-02) compute the same jkt. Accepted: kty OKP/crv Ed25519 (32-byte x, alg EdDSA) and kty EC/crv P-256 (point on the curve, alg ES256). Rejected: RSA, oct, any private or symmetric member (d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, k, oth), x5u, jku and x5c. `use` must be sig and `key_ops` must be [verify] when present; alg defaults from kty/crv and must match when present. kid defaults to the thumbprint and is unique within the agent. At most 2 keys per agent (to allow rotation) and 2 KiB per JWK. Private keys are never accepted, stored or logged.
- Authorization data: allowed_groups uses the same literal, case-sensitive semantics and caps as W-P1-GPOL-01 (trimmed, de-duplicated, sorted, at most 256 values of 256 bytes) and must be non-empty for an active agent. allowed_scopes replaces the old single default_scope: at most 32 values, each matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`; the token service issues allowed_scopes when a request omits scope, and no scope claim when the list is empty. owner_iss/owner_sub default to the creating principal and are informational in P2: they grant no rights, and offboarding an owner does not disable the agent.
- Identity mode is not stored in the registry. The per-agent mode stays in SettingsWire `agents[].identity` (W-P1-VRFY-01) with `identity.defaultMode` as the fallback, so it is versioned, rollback-able and later approvable like other settings. W-P2-WBND-03 adds `require` there. The console shows each agent's effective mode read-only, from live settings.
- Store: `agentreg.Store{Get, List, Create, Update(ctx, a, expectedRevision, actor), SetStatus(ctx, id, status, expectedRevision, actor)}` with errors ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrKeyInUse and a field-scoped ErrInvalid. It is a narrow interface with an exported conformance suite (`agentregtest.Run`) so the P5 Postgres store can implement it. A read-through in-memory cache, invalidated on every write, serves the token service so exchange takes no DB round trip on the hot path.
- Admin API under the P1 console prefix, through a new `dashboard.SetAgentRegistry` seam like the P1 worker-token and blocked-user panels: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/agents`, `GET/PUT /dashboard/api/agents/{id}`, `POST /dashboard/api/agents/{id}/disable` and `/enable`. There is no DELETE. The routes are listed in dashboard.Routes(), so the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table, W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF and W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware apply with no new mount. Viewers read; every write is admin-only, because registering a key or widening allowed_groups decides who can mint agent-bound tokens. Writes require `If-Match: "r<revision>"` (409 `agent_conflict` when stale, 428 when missing). In `console.auth: none` writes return 403 `use_cli`; without --state-dir every route returns 503 `state_dir_required`; on workers the seam is unset and the routes return 404. With W-P2-APIK-02 these rows carry Scope agents:read (GET) and agents:write (writes), so API keys reach the same handlers; there is no /api alias. With approvals enabled, W-P2-APPR-08 holds widening writes as drafts.
- Audit: Target `agents`, Actions agent.create, agent.update, agent.disable and agent.enable, and an `agents` StateHasher (HMAC over the canonical list, W-P1-AAUD-02 pattern). Details hold only changed field names, kids and groups added or removed, and status from/to; never JWK coordinates.
- Worker wire: new `config.RegisteredAgent{ID, Status, JKT []string}` (json `id`, `status`, `jkt`) and `config.Policy.RegisteredAgents` (json `registeredAgents,omitempty`, not accepted in YAML), carried in policyWire and decoded through the existing remoteWire embedding. Owner, groups, scopes and JWK bodies never leave the CP. `policyServer.loadPolicy` merges the store list sorted by id, next to the W-P1-BLOCK-03 blocked-users merge. A store read error fails loadPolicy, so Refresh keeps the last-known-good wire and ETag. One exported `config.ValidateRegisteredAgents` runs in the CP write path and in parseRemotePolicy, so the CP never serves an entry that workers would reject. An empty registry keeps /policy byte-identical.
- Versioning and bundles: registry data is outside policy_versions.doc_json, so a policy rollback never re-enables an agent or restores a removed key. In `--policy-store=versioned` mode an ETag change caused by a registry write appends a policy_publish_log row with reason `agent_registry` (the W-P1-PVER-05 path), so W-P2-SBND-02 bundle numbering stays monotonic; the signed bundle carries the same `registeredAgents` object.
- Worker binding: a new worker-local `central.agentID` YAML key and `warden run --agent-id` flag pin the worker's agent id. Precedence is flag, then central.agentID, then the existing worker.defaultAgentID (Agents[0].ID when exactly one agent is configured, otherwise `agent:<port>`). The resolved id is used everywhere the worker uses defaultAgentID today (judge, identity mode) and for the registry lookup. The worker selects its own RegisteredAgent entry when it applies policy, so the per-request cost is one atomic load. The heartbeat body gains `agentID`, the effective `identityMode` and `caps:["agentreg/v1"]` next to the W-P1-BLOCK-02 caps, which answers the P1 question about reporting each worker's effective identity mode.
- Kill switch (deny-only; it acts only after an admin disables a registered agent, so an empty registry changes nothing): when the worker's bound agent is disabled, every CONNECT, HTTP/1 request and h2 stream gets 403 `{"error":"agent_disabled"}` in every identity mode. Open sessions are closed through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, deny events carry Reason=agent_disabled, and RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") is called. This covers the p1-block-list question about agent-kind block entries. Rejecting tokens whose act.sub is disabled or whose cnf.jkt is no longer registered belongs to W-P2-WBND-02. Default-deny and the secret swap are unchanged.
- Degraded modes: while the CP is down, workers keep the last-known-good registry and never re-enable an agent on their own. Registry state survives CP restarts in SQLite. The fleet view warns when a disabled agent is still served by a worker without `agentreg/v1`, when a registered agent has no bound worker, and when a worker reports an agentID that is not registered. Registry logic does not depend on wall-clock time; created_at and updated_at are informational.
- Offline CLI: `warden control-plane agent register|update|list|disable|enable --state-dir` writes through the same Store and validator and records admin audit rows with auth_method `cli`, so compose recipes, the token-service e2e test and `console.auth: none` deployments can register agents. The running CP picks up CLI writes on its existing 3s policyReloadInterval ticker.
- Observability: bounded labels only. CP: `warden_cp_agents{status}` and `warden_cp_agent_registry_writes_total{action,outcome}`, kept in memory until CP metrics export lands (W-P5-RETN-06). Worker: RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") and a sessions-closed count. Logs carry agent id, kid and thumbprint prefix only, never JWK bodies or tokens.

## Done when

On a CP with --state-dir, console.auth=oidc and console.adminAudit.enabled=true, and one worker started with --agent-id claude-code: an admin registers agent `claude-code` in the console with a public Ed25519 JWK and allowed group `warden-agents`, which writes exactly one admin audit row with target_ref agent:claude-code and no JWK body in the row or logs; a viewer or editor gets 403 on writes, a JWK containing `d` returns 400 and a stale If-Match returns 409; GET /policy carries `registeredAgents` with the agent's id, status and key thumbprint, the worker applies it within one long-poll cycle and reports `agentreg/v1` and its agentID on the heartbeat, and the token service can resolve the agent and key through agentreg.Store; disabling the agent makes that worker answer new and open sessions with 403 agent_disabled within one long-poll cycle in every identity mode, and this still holds after a policy rollback, a CP restart and a CP outage, while re-enabling restores traffic; a CP with an empty registry or without --state-dir serves byte-identical /policy with an unchanged ETag, and old workers decode the new wire without error.

### 1/7 · W-P2-AREG-01

**Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#71](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/71)

Create the new package internal/agentreg with the Agent type, the Store interface, a SQLite implementation on the cpstate DB, and the validators every later ticket shares. JWK parsing and RFC 7638 thumbprints come from internal/keys (W-P2-KEYS-01), so the registry, the token service and workers compute the same jkt. Nothing calls the package yet, so merging changes no behaviour.

**Requirements**

- New `agentid.ValidID(string) error` in internal/agentid with pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$`: `agent:8080` passes, `!identity-scoped`, `-x` and a 65-character id fail.
- `agentreg.Agent{ID, DisplayName, OwnerIss, OwnerSub, OwnerEmail, Keys, AllowedGroups, AllowedScopes, Status, Revision, CreatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedAt, UpdatedBy}`, Status active|disabled, and `config.MaxRegisteredAgents` = 1000 enforced on create. There are no identity_mode or environments fields.
- Key validation through the W-P2-KEYS-01 JWK parser: 1-2 keys; OKP/Ed25519 (alg EdDSA) or EC/P-256 on the curve (alg ES256); RSA, oct, d, p, q, dp, dq, qi, k, oth, x5u, jku and x5c rejected in the raw JSON; `use` sig and `key_ops` [verify] when present; at most 2 KiB per JWK; kid defaults to the thumbprint and is unique within the agent.
- Field validation: allowed_groups normalized like W-P1-GPOL-01 and non-empty for an active agent; allowed_scopes at most 32 values matching `^[a-z0-9:._-]{1,64}$`; display_name at most 128 runes with no control characters. ErrInvalid carries the field path (for example `keys[0].crv`), never the value.
- Migration `agents/0001` creates `agents` and `agent_keys(jkt PK, agent_id, kid, alg, jwk_json)`. Create, Update and SetStatus each run in one transaction; Update and SetStatus use `WHERE revision=?` and return ErrConflict on a stale revision; a jkt already bound to another agent returns ErrKeyInUse. There is no delete path.
- `agentreg.Thumbprints(Agent) []string` is the one projection of key thumbprints used by the wire (W-P2-AREG-04) and the token service. A read-through cache, invalidated on every write, backs Get and List.
- Exported conformance suite `agentregtest.Run(t, Store)` for the P5 Postgres store. Errors and logs carry id, kid and a thumbprint prefix only.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/agentid/agentid.go: add `ValidID` (new) and table tests in agentid_test.go.
2. New internal/agentreg/agent.go: Agent, Status constants, errors (ErrNotFound, ErrConflict, ErrKeyInUse, field-scoped ErrInvalid) and the Store interface.
3. New internal/agentreg/validate.go: `Validate(Agent) (Agent, error)` that normalizes groups and scopes and checks keys with the internal/keys JWK parser and thumbprint from W-P2-KEYS-01; add `Thumbprints`.
4. New internal/agentreg/sqlite.go: `NewSQLiteStore(db *cpstate.DB)` with the `agents/0001` migration registered through the W-P1-SSO-01 migration list, revision compare-and-swap, the jkt uniqueness check and the MaxRegisteredAgents cap; new cache.go for the read-through cache.
5. New internal/agentreg/agentregtest/suite.go: `Run(t, Store)` covering round-trip, conflict, key-in-use, cap and disable.
6. Tests: JWK table tests (private member, wrong curve, RSA, alg mismatch, duplicate kid, 3 keys, x5u), RFC 7638 test vectors, and the conformance suite against the SQLite store.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a JWK containing `d` (or kty oct with `k`), Create returns ErrInvalid naming `keys[0].d` and writes no row.
- [ ] Given an agent with every field set, Create then Get round-trips all fields, kid defaults to the thumbprint and Revision is 1.
- [ ] Given agent A with key K, creating agent B with K returns ErrKeyInUse; Update on A with a stale revision returns ErrConflict.
- [ ] Given SetStatus(id, disabled), Get and List return the agent with status=disabled and the row still exists.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/agentreg/... ./internal/agentid -race` passes and `scripts/check.sh` stays green, including the coverage gate.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#18--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations; [`W-P2-KEYS-01`](key-management.md#17--w-p2-keys-01) Add internal/keys Signer, JWK and RFC 7638 kid helpers

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-AREG-02`](agent-registry.md#27--w-p2-areg-02) Expose the agent registry admin API with admin-only writes and audit; [`W-P2-AREG-04`](agent-registry.md#47--w-p2-areg-04) Serve registered agents in the policy wire; [`W-P2-AREG-06`](agent-registry.md#67--w-p2-areg-06) Add an offline agent registry CLI; [`W-P2-TOKX-01`](token-exchange.md#17--w-p2-tokx-01) Add private_key_jwt client assertion verification

### 2/7 · W-P2-AREG-02

**Expose the agent registry admin API with admin-only writes and audit**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#72](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/72)

Add the agent registry handlers to internal/dashboard behind a new `SetAgentRegistry` seam, mounted under /dashboard/api/agents like the P1 worker-token and blocked-user APIs. Listing them in dashboard.Routes() puts them behind the existing P1 session, CSRF, admin audit and authz chain, so no new middleware mount is needed. Writes are admin-only because a key or group change decides who can mint agent-bound tokens.

**Requirements**

- Routes: `GET /dashboard/api/agents` (200 list), `POST /dashboard/api/agents` (201 with Location), `GET /dashboard/api/agents/{id}` (200 or 404), `PUT /dashboard/api/agents/{id}` (200), `POST /dashboard/api/agents/{id}/disable` and `/enable` (200). There is no DELETE (405).
- Authz entries in the W-P1-SSO-05 table: viewer for GET; admin for every write; Scope (W-P2-APIK-02) agents:read for GET and agents:write for writes, set by whichever of the two tickets lands second. Actions agent.create, agent.update, agent.disable, agent.enable; Target `agents`; Audited true for writes. An `agents` StateHasher is registered with the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware.
- PUT, disable and enable require `If-Match: "r<revision>"`: 428 when missing, 409 `{"error":"agent_conflict"}` when stale. Duplicate id or ErrKeyInUse returns 409; validation returns 400 `{"error":"invalid_agent","field":"keys[0].crv"}`; bodies over 64 KiB return 413.
- Example: `POST /dashboard/api/agents {"id":"claude-code","displayName":"Claude Code","keys":[{"kty":"OKP","crv":"Ed25519","x":"<32-byte b64url>"}],"allowedGroups":["warden-agents"]}` returns 201 `{"id":"claude-code","revision":1,"status":"active","keys":[{"kid":"<jkt>","alg":"EdDSA","jkt":"<jkt>"}],...}` with ETag `"r1"`. Views return public JWKs plus kid, alg and jkt only.
- `console.auth: none`: writes return 403 `{"error":"use_cli"}`, reads are allowed. CP without --state-dir: every route returns 503 `{"error":"state_dir_required"}`. Worker dashboards never set the seam, so the routes return 404.
- Handlers call `adminaudit.Annotate(ctx, "agent:<id>", details)` with an allowlist: changed field names, kids added and removed, groups added and removed, status from/to. No JWK coordinates appear in details, logs or errors. Every successful write calls `Server.refresh()`.
- owner_iss, owner_sub and owner_email default to the calling Principal on create; in-memory counters `warden_cp_agent_registry_writes_total{action,outcome}` and a `warden_cp_agents{status}` gauge are kept for W-P5-RETN-06.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/dashboard/dashboard_agents.go: an `AgentRegistry` interface over dashboard view types (dashboard does not import agentreg or controlplane), `Server.SetAgentRegistry` (new) and the handlers, with If-Match parsing and the error mapping.
2. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: register the routes in Handler() next to the other /dashboard/api/* routes and add them to `dashboard.Routes()`.
3. New internal/controlplane/agents.go: adapter from agentreg.Store to dashboard.AgentRegistry, the `agents` StateHasher, the authz table entries, the none-mode and no-state-dir responses and the in-memory counters.
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add `Config.AgentStore agentreg.Store`; in Handler() call `dash.SetAgentRegistry` on the CP only. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go builds the store from `Config.State` when --state-dir is set.
5. Tests: internal/dashboard/dashboard_agents_test.go (status codes, If-Match, 404 with no seam) and internal/controlplane/agents_test.go with a fake session principal and the adminaudit store (role table, one audit row per write, no key material in details_json, route-coverage test).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a viewer or editor session, POST and PUT on /dashboard/api/agents return 403 role_required; given an admin, create, update, disable and enable each append exactly one admin_audit row with target_ref `agent:<id>` and no `x` or `y` member in details_json.
- [ ] Given a JWK with crv P-384, POST returns 400 with field `keys[0].crv`; a PUT with a stale If-Match returns 409 and a PUT without If-Match returns 428.
- [ ] Given a POST from an admin session without X-Warden-CSRF, the response is 403 and the audit row has outcome denied.
- [ ] Given `console.auth: none`, POST returns 403 use_cli; given no --state-dir, GET returns 503 state_dir_required; on a worker dashboard the routes return 404.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane -race -run 'TestAgents|TestAuthzRouteCoverage'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-AREG-01`](agent-registry.md#17--w-p2-areg-01) Add internal/agentreg store, schema and validation; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#58--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#24--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-AREG-03`](agent-registry.md#37--w-p2-areg-03) Add the Agents tab to the CP console; [`W-P2-AREG-04`](agent-registry.md#47--w-p2-areg-04) Serve registered agents in the policy wire; [`W-P2-APPR-08`](policy-approvals.md#89--w-p2-appr-08) Hold block-list removals and widening agent edits for approval; [`W-P2-WBND-07`](identity-enforcement.md#710--w-p2-wbnd-07) Refuse require mode for agents served by workers without the capability

### 3/7 · W-P2-AREG-03

**Add the Agents tab to the CP console**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#73](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/73)

Add an Agents tab to internal/dashboard/index.html that calls the W-P2-AREG-02 endpoints through the P1 `api()` wrapper. It lists agents, creates and edits them with a pasted public JWK, disables and re-enables them, and shows each agent's effective identity mode and bound workers read-only. The CP also decodes the new heartbeat fields from W-P2-AREG-05 so the fleet view can show bindings; the tab adds no Go writer seam.

**Requirements**

- `/dashboard/api/setup` (handleSetup in dashboard_v3.go) gains `agentRegistry: true` only when the AgentRegistry seam is set and the CP has a state dir; the tab is hidden otherwise, including on every worker.
- The list shows id, display name, owner email, allowed groups, allowed scopes, key kids with alg and an 8-character jkt prefix, status, revision, the effective identity mode (from live settings agents[].identity, else identity.defaultMode) and the workers whose heartbeat agentID matches. JWK coordinates are never shown in the list.
- The form takes a pasted public JWK (up to 2, for rotation), groups and scopes; it refuses client-side a JWK with a `d` member, sends If-Match with the revision, shows a 400 field error inline and on 409 offers a reload.
- Write controls are shown only when /auth/me reports admin; the server stays the only enforcement point.
- handleHeartbeat decodes optional `agentID` (agentid.ValidID, else dropped) and `identityMode` (bounded enum) next to the W-P1-BLOCK-04 caps; WorkerRegistry stores them and WorkerView exposes them. Old heartbeats keep working. Warnings: a disabled agent still served by a worker without `agentreg/v1`, a registered agent with no bound worker, and a worker reporting an unregistered agentID.
- Every user-supplied value is rendered with textContent only.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go handleSetup: add the agentRegistry flag, read from the seam state.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go handleHeartbeat and registry.go: decode and store agentID and identityMode; internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: add them to WorkerView.
3. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the Agents tab, list view, create/edit form and disable/enable buttons with a confirm dialog, using the W-P1-SSO-04 `api()` wrapper.
4. internal/dashboard/index.html: join the agent list with the fleet view (WorkerView caps and agentID) to render bound workers and the warnings.
5. Tests in internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go (setup flag on and off, index contains the tab markup, list response with no JWK `x` member) and internal/controlplane (heartbeat with and without agentID, invalid agentID dropped).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an admin on the CP, an agent created in the tab is returned by GET /dashboard/api/agents with the same id, groups and kid.
- [ ] Given a worker dashboard, /dashboard/api/setup returns agentRegistry=false and the tab is not rendered.
- [ ] Given display_name `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`, the list renders it as text.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestSetupAgentRegistry|TestIndexAgentsTab'` and `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestHeartbeatAgentFields` pass.

### 4/7 · W-P2-AREG-04

**Serve registered agents in the policy wire**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#74](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/74)

Add `registeredAgents` (id, status and key thumbprints) to the /policy wire, merged in policyServer.loadPolicy from the agent store, and decode it on workers through the existing remoteWire embedding with one shared validator. Following the block-list pattern, a store error keeps the last-known-good wire, an empty registry keeps /policy byte-identical, and registry data stays out of policy versions. Workers only store the list in this ticket; enforcement is W-P2-AREG-05.

**Requirements**

- internal/config: new `RegisteredAgent{ID, Status, JKT []string}` (json `id`, `status`, `jkt`) and `Policy.RegisteredAgents` (json `registeredAgents,omitempty`; not added to rawConfig, so YAML cannot set it). Policy.DeepCopy copies it.
- New exported `config.ValidateRegisteredAgents`: ids pass agentid.ValidID and are unique, status is active or disabled, at most 2 jkt per agent each 43 base64url characters and unique across agents, at most MaxRegisteredAgents entries. It runs in parseRemotePolicy (after sorting by id) and in the CP before serving.
- controlplane.policyWire gains `RegisteredAgents []config.RegisteredAgent` json `registeredAgents,omitempty`, projected with agentreg.Thumbprints; owner, groups, scopes and JWKs are never included.
- policyServer gets an optional registry source; loadPolicy merges it, sorted by id, in both the file and versioned serve paths. A read or validation error fails loadPolicy, so Refresh keeps the previous wire and ETag and logs one `agentreg_load_failed` line with no entry values.
- Registry data is excluded from policy_versions.doc_json. In versioned mode an ETag change caused by a registry write appends a policy_publish_log row with reason `agent_registry` through the W-P1-PVER-05 AppendPublish path.
- Writes from AREG-02 call Server.refresh(); writes from the offline CLI are picked up by the existing 3s policyReloadInterval ticker.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/config.go (or new internal/config/registered_agents.go): RegisteredAgent, Policy.RegisteredAgents, DeepCopy and ValidateRegisteredAgents.
2. internal/config/remote.go parseRemotePolicy: sort and validate RegisteredAgents before `validate`; an invalid list rejects the whole wire like other invalid policy.
3. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add the field to policyWire. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: add the optional source and a new `withRegisteredAgents(wire)` helper called at the end of loadPolicy, next to the W-P1-BLOCK-03 `withBlockedUsers`.
4. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go Refresh: when the ETag changes without a version create and the registered-agent list changed, call AppendPublish with reason `agent_registry`.
5. Tests in internal/config (remote_test.go fixtures with and without the key, validation table, DeepCopy under -race) and internal/controlplane (golden /policy bytes and ETag with an empty registry, long-poll wake on write, store error keeps ETag, rollback keeps a disabled agent disabled, publish_log row).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an empty registry or no --state-dir, /policy bytes and ETag equal the pre-change golden.
- [ ] Given a worker blocked on GET /policy?wait= with the current ETag, an admin disable returns the long-poll with a new ETag within 1s and the entry shows status=disabled.
- [ ] Given the store returns an error, the served ETag and wire stay unchanged.
- [ ] Given `--policy-store=versioned`, a rollback to a version from before the disable leaves the agent disabled in the served wire, and the disable wrote one publish_log row with reason agent_registry.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/config -run TestRegisteredAgents` and `go test ./internal/controlplane -race -run 'TestPolicyWireRegisteredAgents|TestLongPollWakesOnAgentWrite'` pass.

### 5/7 · W-P2-AREG-05

**Bind workers to an agent id and enforce agent_disabled**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#250](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/250)

Let an operator pin a worker to a registered agent id with `--agent-id` or `central.agentID`, and make a disabled agent a deny-only kill switch on that worker. The worker denies every CONNECT, request and h2 stream with 403 agent_disabled in every identity mode, and closes open sessions through the P1 session registry within one long-poll cycle. The heartbeat reports the resolved agent id, the effective identity mode and the `agentreg/v1` capability so the fleet view can flag workers that do not enforce it. This is worker-lane only; with no flag and an empty registry nothing changes.

**Requirements**

- New worker-local `central.agentID` YAML key (next to central.proxyID in internal/config/central.go) and `warden run --agent-id` flag. Precedence: flag, then central.agentID, then worker.defaultAgentID. A value that fails agentid.ValidID stops startup with a clear error. The resolved id replaces defaultAgentID everywhere (judge, identity mode lookup, registry lookup).
- On every policy apply the worker selects its own RegisteredAgent entry and stores `disabled bool` in an atomic value read by the proxy; the per-request check is one atomic load with no allocation.
- When the bound agent is disabled: CONNECT is answered 403 before any dial or `200 Connection Established`, HTTP/1 requests are answered in a new `agentStage` before judgeGate, and each h2 stream gets 403 in serveGRPCStream. The body is `{"error":"agent_disabled"}`; the event has Decision=deny and Reason=agent_disabled; RecordBlocked("agent_disabled") is called. `agent_disabled` is added to internal/proxy/reasons.go (W-P1-JAUD-06).
- After each applied policy change that disables the bound agent, the worker closes every open session (tunnels, keep-alive, h2, WebSocket) through the W-P1-BLOCK-05 session registry, including sessions with no identity, and writes one deny event per closed session.
- The heartbeat body (RemoteProvider.Heartbeat) gains `agentID`, `identityMode` (the effective P1 mode) and `agentreg/v1` in `caps`; it stays under the CP's 4096-byte limit. The CP side that stores and shows these fields is W-P2-AREG-03, so this ticket changes no CP code.
- A worker never re-enables a disabled agent on its own: while the CP is unreachable it keeps the last-known-good list. Logs carry the agent id only, never thumbprints at info level.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/central.go: add AgentID to the central config and raw struct. cmd/proxy/run.go: add the `--agent-id` flag and pass it into worker options.
2. internal/worker/judge.go: new `resolveAgentID(flag, central string, pol config.Policy, listenAddr string)` wrapping defaultAgentID; use it at the existing defaultAgentID call site and in the identity mode lookup.
3. internal/proxy: add an atomic agent-status holder with `SetAgentDisabled(bool)`; deny in handleConn (serve.go), a new agentStage in runRequestStages (http.go) and serveGRPCStream (grpc.go) via a new `denyAgentDisabled` helper; add the reason constant.
4. internal/proxy/sessions.go (W-P1-BLOCK-05): add `CloseAllSessions(reason)` that also covers anonymous sessions when the agent is disabled, by tracking every session while a registry entry exists for the bound agent.
5. internal/worker/loops.go: in the afterReplace hook, select the bound RegisteredAgent, call SetAgentDisabled and close sessions on an active-to-disabled change.
6. internal/config/remote.go Heartbeat: add agentID, identityMode and the `agentreg/v1` cap to the W-P1-BLOCK-02 body struct.
7. Tests in internal/proxy (CONNECT deny with zero dials, kept-alive request denied after the change, h2 stream 403, open tunnel closed), internal/worker (flag precedence, apply hook) and internal/config (heartbeat body fields and size).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given `--agent-id claude-code` and central.agentID `other`, the worker resolves `claude-code`; with neither set it resolves the same id as defaultAgentID today.
- [ ] Given the bound agent becomes disabled while a CONNECT tunnel and an h2 connection are open, both are closed within one long-poll cycle, and a new CONNECT gets 403 agent_disabled with zero upstream dials.
- [ ] Given identity modes off, attribute and (after W-P2-WBND-03) require, a disabled agent is denied in each; re-enabling restores traffic on the next apply.
- [ ] Given a worker with --agent-id claude-code, the heartbeat body it sends contains agentID `claude-code`, its effective identityMode and `agentreg/v1` in caps, and is under 4096 bytes.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy ./internal/worker -race -run 'TestAgentDisabled|TestResolveAgentID'` and `go test ./internal/config -run TestHeartbeatAgent` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-AREG-04`](agent-registry.md#47--w-p2-areg-04) Serve registered agents in the policy wire; [`W-P1-BLOCK-02`](user-block-list.md#27--w-p1-block-02) Enforce the block list in the worker at CONNECT, per request and per h2 stream; [`W-P1-BLOCK-05`](user-block-list.md#57--w-p1-block-05) Close open sessions of newly blocked users on policy change; [`W-P1-VRFY-02`](identity-verification.md#27--w-p1-vrfy-02) Extract, verify and strip identity on CONNECT, HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2

### 6/7 · W-P2-AREG-06

**Add an offline agent registry CLI**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#251](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/251)

Add `warden control-plane agent register|update|list|disable|enable --state-dir` so agents can be registered without the console. Compose recipes, the token-service e2e test and `console.auth: none` deployments (where console writes return use_cli) need a scriptable path. The CLI uses the same Store and validator and records admin audit rows like the console.

**Requirements**

- `agent register --id ID --jwk-file F [--jwk-file F2] --groups g1,g2 [--scopes s1,s2] [--display-name N]`, `agent update --id ID --revision N ...`, `agent list [--json]`, `agent disable --id ID --revision N` and `agent enable --id ID --revision N`; each requires --state-dir and works with or without a running CP.
- --jwk-file accepts a public JWK or a JWKS as printed by `warden identity enroll` (W-P2-RCP-01); a file containing a private member is refused with the field path and nothing else from the file is printed.
- Each write appends an admin audit row through the W-P1-AAUD-01 Recorder with auth_method `cli` and actor `cli:<os user>`, with the same details allowlist as W-P2-AREG-02; when admin audit is not enabled the command still works and logs a warning.
- `list` prints id, status, revision, kids and an 8-character jkt prefix, never JWK coordinates. Exit code is non-zero on any validation error, conflict or key-in-use.
- A running CP serves CLI writes within one policyReloadInterval (3s).

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the `agent` subcommand group under `control-plane`, opening cpstate the same way as the W-P1-WTOK-05 token commands.
2. New cmd/proxy/controlplane_agent.go: flag parsing, JWK file loading and calls into agentreg.Store and the admin audit Recorder.
3. Tests in cmd/proxy/controlplane_test.go: register, list, disable with a stale revision, private-key refusal and audit row written.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a state dir, `warden control-plane agent register --id claude-code --jwk-file pub.json --groups warden-agents --state-dir d` exits 0 and `agent list --json --state-dir d` shows the agent with status active and revision 1.
- [ ] Given a JWK file containing `d`, register exits non-zero naming `keys[0].d` and writes no row.
- [ ] Given a running CP on the same state dir, a CLI disable appears in GET /policy within 3s.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneAgent` passes.

### 7/7 · W-P2-AREG-07

**Document the agent registry and add an end-to-end test**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#252](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/252)

Write the operator docs for the agent registry and add an integration test that runs a CP and a bound worker, registers an agent, disables it and checks that the worker denies and then recovers. This proves the done-when sentence on a real process pair and records the identity-mode and binding rules in one place.

**Requirements**

- docs/control-plane.md gains an Agent registry section: id format, JWK rules and 2-key rotation, admin-only writes, If-Match, the offline CLI and the none-mode rule, worker binding precedence (`--agent-id`, central.agentID, defaultAgentID), the kill switch, and that the identity mode lives in settings agents[].identity, not in the registry.
- The docs state what survives what: a policy rollback never re-enables an agent, a CP outage keeps the last-known-good list, and old workers without `agentreg/v1` do not enforce disable.
- New integration test under the `integration` build tag in test/integration: start a CP with a temp --state-dir and a worker with `--agent-id claude-code`, register the agent with the CLI, assert traffic flows, disable it, assert 403 agent_disabled on a new CONNECT and closure of an open tunnel, re-enable and assert recovery.
- The test asserts that no JWK coordinate appears in captured CP or worker logs.
- The test is hermetic: loopback only, no external network, under 60s.

**Implementation plan**

1. docs/control-plane.md: add the Agent registry section and a row to the worker-to-control-plane interactions list for `registeredAgents` and the heartbeat fields.
2. test/integration/agentreg_test.go (new): the end-to-end flow using the existing integration helpers in integration_test.go.
3. configs/config.example.yaml: add a commented `central.agentID` example.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestAgentRegistryKillSwitch` passes locally and in CI.
- [ ] docs/control-plane.md describes the binding precedence and the kill switch, and `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` still passes.
- [ ] Captured logs in the test contain no `"x":` JWK member.
